_about: Developer experience frameworks for the Kite Pulse guides: SPACE, the DevEx framework and DX Core 4. Every dimension and example metric carries the exact wording it was taken from and its source. Read by /blog/developer-experience-metrics (copied into the prototype's FRAMEWORKS and METRICS on the checked date). The two papers were read from their PDFs because the ACM sites refuse automated reads. Frameworks change slowly; re-check yearly, and DX Core 4 whenever DX revises it.
not_used: DX's reported outcomes for DX Core 4 (efficiency gains, engagement): vendor-reported, seen in search results only
DX Core 4 benchmark values (e.g. diffs per engineer by quartile): vendor benchmarks, not read on a primary page, and the page is not a benchmark

space.citation: Forsgren, Storey, Maddila, Zimmermann, Houck, Butler. The SPACE of Developer Productivity. ACM Queue 19(1), 2021; Communications of the ACM 64(6), June 2021.
space.single_metric: it cannot be measured by a single metric or activity data alone
space.at_least_three: teams and leaders (and even individuals) should capture several metrics across multiple dimensions of the framework—at least three are recommended
space.perceptual: Another recommendation is that at least one of the metrics include perceptual measures such as survey data.
space.activity_warning: they should never be used in isolation to make decisions about individual or team productivity because of their known limitations
space.aggregate: report only anonymized, aggregate results at the team or group level

Satisfaction and well-being: Developer efficacy. Whether developers have the tools and resources they need to get their work done.
Burnout. Exhaustion caused by excessive and prolonged workplace stress.
Performance: Quality. Reliability, absence of bugs, ongoing service health.
Impact. Customer satisfaction, customer adoption and retention, feature usage, cost reduction.
Activity: Design and coding. Volume or count of design documents and specs, work items, pull requests, commits, and code reviews.
Communication and collaboration: Onboarding time for and experience of new members.
Efficiency and flow: Number of handoffs in a process
Perceived ability to stay in flow and complete work.
Interruptions: quantity, timing, how spaced, impact on development work and flow.
Time measures through a system: total time, value-added time, wait time.

devex.citation: Noda, Storey, Forsgren, Greiler. DevEx: What Actually Drives Productivity. ACM Queue 21(2), March-April 2023.
devex.definition: Developer experience encompasses how developers feel about, think about, and value their work.
devex.dimensions: Our framework distills developer experience to its three core dimensions: feedback loops, cognitive load, and flow state
devex.feedback_loops: the speed and quality of responses to actions performed
devex.cognitive_load: Cognitive load encompasses the amount of mental processing required for a developer to perform a task.
devex.flow_state: a mental state in which a person performing an activity is fully immersed in a feeling of energized focus, full involvement, and enjoyment
devex.neither_alone: A comparative analysis of perceptual measures and workflows is necessary because neither alone can tell the full picture.

feedback_loops: Satisfaction with automated test speed and output
Satisfaction with time it takes to validate a local change
Satisfaction with time it takes to deploy a change to production
flow_state: Perceived ability to focus and avoid interruptions
Satisfaction with clarity of task or project goals

feedback_loops: Time it takes to generate CI results
Deployment lead time (time it takes to get a change released to production)
cognitive_load: Time it takes to get answers to technical questions
Manual steps required to deploy a change
flow_state: Number of blocks of time without meetings or interruptions
Frequency of unplanned tasks or requests
Frequency of incidents requiring team attention

kpis: Overall perceived ease of delivering software

dx_core4.citation: Abi Noda. Introducing the DX Core 4. DX newsletter, 10 December 2024.

key_metrics.Speed: Diffs per Engineer (or PRs per Engineer)
key_metrics.Impact: Percentage of Time Spent on New Capabilities

dx_core4.dxi: an aggregated score from 14 standardized Likert-scale survey items
dx_core4.diffs_warning: It is critical that this metric is never used at the individual level or tied to performance evaluations.
